NHS England has built the digital flag into the NHS Spine to enable health and social care professionals to record, share and review details of reasonable adjustment across health and publicity funded social care, wherever the person is treated nationwide.

The Reasonable Adjustment Digital Flag is a visible marker on a patient's record which identifies the changes that need to be made by health and care services to make services as accessible for disabled people as they are for everyone else.

The Equality Act 2010 [3] states that organisations must make reasonable adjustments for disabled persons to make access to services equitable.

If you feel your needs requires a reasonable adjustment, example, easy read leaflets, appointment letter, large font leaflets, appointments letters, a British Sign Language Interpreter, A quitter room for you to wait in, wheelchair accessibility, offer of an appointment at ground floor level, to be seen with your carer or support, please speak to our reception team who will be happy to assist you in this.  This information will also be captured in any routine appointment, health check appointment etc, we are also changing our new patient registration forms to include this information.

We will require patients consent for all reasonable adjustment flag to be added.

Dementia and dehydration in hot weather
Text/Information to be posted:
Dehydration is a common challenge for older people, and especially those with dementia. Memory problems mean someone with dementia can easily forget to drink enough water.

What’s more, the part of the brain that recognises you’re dehydrated and sends a message to let you know you’re thirsty doesn’t always work properly. Some medications and dementia-related illnesses can also make dehydration worse.

Our dementia advisers are here for you.
0333 150 3456
5 tips for preventing dehydration
Here are some simple but effective ways of helping to prevent dehydration during hot weather:

Leave beakers or jugs of water within easy reach. This is especially important for people with limited mobility, who aren’t able to get up and make themselves a drink.
Make drinking easier. Have a clear beaker so the person can see what’s inside (this may not work so well with water) or a brightly coloured cup to draw attention. Make sure the beaker is within the line of sight. Having a beaker that is suitable (not too heavy or an odd shape) can help. Straws might also be a good idea.
Share a drink together. Have a cup of tea or a soft drink with the person and make sure they're drinking during mealtimes.
Leave prompts and reminders. Make sure the person with dementia remembers to drink regularly by leaving notes out for them or putting up notices around the house. You could also set up a phone reminder or set an alarm clock.
Provide high water content foods. Supplement water and other drinks with foods that are high in fluids. Some good options include ice lollies, jelly, ice cream, soup and fruit such as melon. ‘Water sweets’, such as Jelly Drops, can also help the person stay hydrated.

A message from NHS Surrey

We have been made aware that a scam e-mail has been sent out to people living in Sussex inviting them to update their details in order to remain registered with their GP practice.  We wanted to warn Surrey residents in case they also receive a similar scam email.

This is a generic scam e-mail which directs people to install software by clicking on a button which says 'I don't want to change my GP' and then providing their contact details.  Should you get this scam email, do not do this.

There is no programme of work being undertaken locally, or nationally, to ask you to confirm your registration details using additional software.

Sometimes, practices may ask you to confirm your contact details as it is important that you keep these up to date. However, if your GP practice wanted to check this with you, you would be contacted directly by them and not generically.

You find out more information and advice on how to identify fraud and can report scam e-mails via Action Fraud https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/report-phishing.

Text/Information to be posted:
You might have seen online or on the news that GPs can now give out a medicine called tirzepatide (Mounjaro®) on the NHS to help people lose weight. While this is true in some parts of the country, it’s not yet available in South Yorkshire.

 

That’s because the people in charge are still making plans for how the service will work. This includes making sure additional support for physical activity, diet and nutrition is ready too.

 

We know this might be disappointing, but we ask for your patience while everything is being sorted out.

 

It’s also important to know that not everyone will be able to get tirzepatide, even if they want it. The NHS has very strict rules about who can have it, and some people might not meet those rules—even though the medicine is approved.

 

In the meantime, we’re here to help. Please keep talking to us about the other ways we can support your weight loss journey. And we’ll let you know as soon as there are any updates.

 

Thank you for understanding.

From 23rd June the new weight loss injectable drug will become available on the NHS, this will be rolled out at first to patients with the highest clinical need. 
The first group will be patients with a BMI of 40 and 4 or more of the following conditions:
- Type 2 diabetes
- High blood pressure
- Heart disease
- Obstructive sleep apnoea
- Abnormal blood fats
Patients who meet this criteria will be identified and contacted by the NHS to offer them this treatment once the service is up and running. 
It will not be delivered by your local medical practice and the criteria is strict so you do not need to contact your medical practice to enquire about it for the timebeing as the NHS will contact you if you are in the high priority group.
For more information please follow the link below:
https://www.england.nhs.uk/ourwork/prevention/obesity/medicines-for-obesity/weight-management-injections/

Text/Information to be posted: -Patient Information – Mounjaro (tirzepatide) for Weight Loss You may have seen recent media reports stating that GPs can now prescribe weight-loss injections like Mounjaro. While this is true nationally, in our area (Suffolk and North East Essex), *GPs are not commissioned to provide these medications directly for weight loss*. Instead, the local NHS has chosen a Community Outreach service model. This means: Access is only available through a specialist NHS weight management service (WMCOS). This is not currently operating at present. Patients must be clinically assessed to determine eligibility. GP Funding. Do You Know The Facts?
Text/Information to be posted:
Here at Foxhill Medical Centre we continually strive to offer excellent care to our patients. 
We are very proud of our team, our beautiful building and the services we provide, but are you aware of how much a GP practice is actually paid per patient per day to provide health care? Well, not a much as you may think.
It does not matter how many times a patient attends, we receive only 31p per person per day to provide all of their care. That is less than the cost of an apple.
Out of this, we pay our own rent, energy bills, buy our own equipment, pay for our GP's, nurses, managers, receptionists, administrators & cleaners. 
It really does require lots of careful budgeting and planning but we always do our very best with what we have. 
That is why it is essential that we protect what we have and don't abuse it. Lets take care of our primary care services and the amazing people who work so hard to provide medical care in the most challenging of times.

The partnership, launched on 27 May 2025, offers urgent mental health support by text message to people in South Yorkshire
Anyone in the area experiencing anxiety, stress, loneliness, depression, self-harm, suicidal thoughts, or other mental health challenges can use the service by texting the word ‘EYUP’ to 85258 at any time of day or night. 

The text service is designed to provide anonymous support for people who need urgent mental health assistance. The service ensures patients can access help, day or night, without having to wait to speak to someone face-to-face or on the telephone. As well as providing support to members of the public, it also helps ease pressures on mental health services. 

From 27 May, to start a conversation: 
•	Text the word ‘EYUP’ to 85258 
•	You’ll receive four automated messages before being connected to one of Shout’s qualified mental health professionals  
•	Once connected, the mental health professional will listen empathetically, provide support and signpost to local services where appropriate 

The Shout service is free, anonymous, and does not appear on phone bills. Users do not need to register, download an app, or use mobile data.

What is a PPG?

A Patient Participation Group is a group of patients, carers, and practice staff who meet regularly to discuss and influence the services provided by the practice. It is a great opportunity for you to have your say and make a difference in how healthcare is delivered in your community.

Why Join Our PPG?

•	Have Your Voice Heard: Share your ideas and feedback on how we can improve our services.

•	Stay Informed: Get updates on changes and developments within the practice.
•	Build Community: Connect with other patients and practice staff.

Missed appointments waste huge amounts of time and effort. Nationally, missed appointments cost the NHS over half a billion pounds a year, which is enough to run two hospitals. If every appointment is 10 minutes long that equates to 35 hours a month lost to patients not cancelling their appointments.

 

Please help us this winter by cancelling your appointments.

Carers Week is an annual campaign to raise awareness of caring, highlight the challenges unpaid carers face and recognise the contribution they make to families and communities throughout the UK. It also helps people who don't think of themselves as having caring responsibilities to identify as carers and access much-needed support.
 
A carer is anyone who looks after a family member or friend who has a disability, mental or physical illness, addiction, or who needs extra help as they grow older. The impact of caring on all aspects of life from relationships and health to finances and work can be significant. Whilst many feel that caring is one of the most important things they do, its challenges should not be underestimated. Caring without the right information and support can be tough. It is vitally important that we recognise the contribution carers make to their families and local communities, workplaces and society, and that they get the support they need.
 
Carers need to be recognised for the difficulties they are experiencing, respected for all they are doing, provided with information, and given the support they need to care safely. 
 
The theme for Carers Week 2025 is 'Caring About Equality', calling for an equal society where carers are truly valued, recognised and supported. 
 
Please come along and speak with members of our staff and our partner organisations who can give you information, advice and support around supporting Carers.

The percentage of inactive adults in Doncaster has decreased by 0.2 percentage points to 30.3%

The partnership, launched on 27 May 2025, offers urgent mental health support by text message to people in South Yorkshire.

 

The service – a partnership between NHS South Yorkshire and innovative digital service Shout, which is powered by the charity Mental Health Innovations – offers free, confidential, 24/7 text support for anyone struggling to cope.

 

Anyone in the area experiencing anxiety, stress, loneliness, depression, self-harm, suicidal thoughts, or other mental health challenges can use the service by texting the word ‘EYUP’ to 85258 at any time of day or night.

 

The text service is designed to provide anonymous support for people who need urgent mental health assistance. The service ensures patients can access help, day or night, without having to wait to speak to someone face-to-face or on the telephone. As well as providing support to members of the public, it also helps ease pressures on mental health services.

 

From 27 May, to start a conversation:

Text the word ‘EYUP’ to 85258
You’ll receive four automated messages before being connected to one of Shout’s qualified mental health professionals
Once connected, the mental health professional will listen empathetically, provide support and signpost to local services where appropriate

 

The Shout service is free, anonymous, and does not appear on phone bills. Users do not need to register, download an app, or use mobile data.

You will find a comms toolkit here which includes social media assets, posters, screen assets, information cards, flyers and web banners. Where appropriate, please share these through your channels.

We know it’s not always ‘back to normal’ when you finish hospital treatment for primary breast cancer. Coping with the shock of a diagnosis, treatment and side effects, and worries about recurrence can make it difficult to readjust to the everyday.

Our Moving Forward courses run over two half-day sessions on consecutive weeks. Groups are kept small, with no more than 12–15 people attending. Each course has a Q&A session with one of our healthcare professionals, an expert facilitator, as well as our trained volunteers. Moving Forward is supported by our Journal and online platform which means you can find the answers to the questions that are important to you.

You can attend Moving Forward either at our face-to-face or online courses. Find a course near you or register for an online course at Moving Forward call us on 0345 077 1893.

Know your Numbers Week (Blood Pressure): 8th-14th September 2025
Every September, blood pressure checks are taken by thousands to prevent heart attacks and strokes.
Around 5 million adults aged 18–64 in the UK could be living with undiagnosed high blood pressure – a major risk factor for stroke, heart attack, kidney disease, and early death. Often called the ‘silent killer’, high blood pressure has no symptoms, yet it is the single biggest preventable cause of death in the UK.
Know your Numbers Week aims to reach those who have high blood pressure but are not aware, so that they can get the support they need to bring it under control.
High blood pressure is very common, especially in older adults. There are usually no symptoms, so you may not realise you have it.
Things that increase your chances of having high blood pressure include:
•	Your age – you’re more likely to get high blood pressure as you get older
•	Having close relatives with high blood pressure
•	Your ethnicity – you’re at higher risk if you have a Black African, Black Caribbean or South Asian ethnic background
•	Having an unhealthy diet – especially a diet that’s high in salt
•	Being overweight
•	Smoking
•	Drinking too much alcohol
•	Feeling stressed over a long period

Emergency Alerts  is a UK government service that will warn you if there’s a danger to life nearby. In an emergency, such as severe flooding, fires or extreme weather, your mobile phone or tablet will receive an alert with advice about how to stay safe.
On Sunday 7 September at 3pm, UK Government will be testing emergency alert system (EAS) for the second-ever nationwide test.
The test causes a mobile phone or tablet to:
•	make a loud siren-like sound that lasts about 10 seconds, even if it's set on silent,
•	It may also cause a device to vibrate or read out the alert.
•	A message will appear on your screens making it clear the alert is only a test.
Find out more about the Emergency Alerts on GOV.UK. Emergency Alert Test: Frequently Asked Questions - GOV.UK

If you are affected by domestic abuse and have a concealed mobile phone from your abuser, you may not wish the sound of the alert to draw attention to your phone.

Harewood Medical Practice now have a Patient POD installed.
The Patient Pod Healthcare System is designed to enhance
patient care delivery, improve appointment capacity, and
improve health outcomes. The Patient Pod is equipped with
integrated health monitoring systems, and is a safe
environment for patients, particularly in managing long-term
conditions, ongoing care and post-operative care.
The patient pod will measure and record the following:
• Blood Pressure
• Pulse Rate
• Weight
• Height
• Body Mass index

The monitors are extremely user friendly, with visual and audio step by step instructions.
The information will then be reviewed by a clinician and all findings will be automatically record in the patient records. If the clinician need to follow up on any of the results a member of the
practice team will contact the patient directly.

So we can keep all of our patient records upto date and enable us to monitor the health of all of our patients we would like everyone aged 18 years and over to come in and use the patient POD at any time that practice is open.

Every time you come for an appointment, arrive 15 minutes early (10 minutes to rest) and go and use the POD.
If you are going shopping and have a few minutes spare pop into the practice and use the POD…. You don’t need an appointment.
The team will be on hand to help you use it especially if its your first time

Our aim is for every patient over 18 years of age to use the POD at least once a year

Changes in COVID-19 vaccination eligibility for autumn/winter 2025/26
•        Every year, the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) considers who needs to be vaccinated, to help protect people from serious illness. 
•        This autumn/winter, vaccination is being offered only to people at highest risk of serious illness - older people and those who have a weakened immune system because of a health condition or treatment. This is different to previous years.
•        It’s possible for you to be eligible for a flu vaccine but not eligible for COVID-19 vaccination, even if you’ve had it previously.
•        For autumn/winter vaccination invitations, NHS England uses information from NHS records to check who is eligible for vaccination.
•        Information in these records may no longer be relevant if the health condition has resolved or the diagnosis or medicines has changed.
 
You can get the autumn/ winter COVID-19 vaccine if you:
•	are aged 75 or over (including those who will be 75 by 31 January 2026)
•	are aged 6 months to 74 years and have a weakened immune system because of a health condition or treatment (see below)
•	live in a care home for older adults
You may be eligible for a COVID-19 vaccine if you have a weakened immune system because of a health condition or treatment. This can include if you:
•	have or had blood cancer, such as leukaemia, lymphoma or myeloma
•	have had an organ transplant, bone marrow transplant or stem cell transplant
•	have HIV
•	have a genetic disorder that affects your immune system, such as severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)
•	are having or recently had chemotherapy, biological therapy or radiotherapy
•	are taking steroid medicine (depending on the dose)

The shingles vaccine helps protect against shingles. It’s available on the NHS for:
All adults turning 65
Those aged 70 to 79
Those aged 18 and over with a severely weakened immune system

What the shingles vaccine is for
Shingles is a common condition that causes a painful rash. It can sometimes lead to serious problems such as long-lasting pain, hearing loss or blindness.

You’re more likely to get shingles, and it’s more likely to cause serious problems, as you get older or if you have a severely weakened immune system.

The shingles vaccine helps:

Reduce your chances of getting shingles
Reduce your chances of getting serious problems if you do get shingles.

You will need 2 doses of Shingrix for the best protection. We will contact you (if eligible) to make an appointment.

For more information please see https://www.nhs.uk/vaccinations/shingles-vaccine/

Text/Information to be posted:
My name is Jenny, I am a practice nurse here at Mosslands Medical Practice and I take the lead at the surgery for being the point of contact and facilitating reviews for our patients with learning disabilities and their parents and carers. I recognise the health inequalities that patients with learning disabilities can have and wanted to do something to tackle this. I decided to introduce an Arts and Craft evening with the help of my valued colleagues, held here at the surgery, every four weeks. This was a view to build relationships, rapport and trust with our learning disability patients whilst trying to give them a fun, stimulating session! Also, importantly, to provide their parents and carers a little respite time to themselves.

The group started in May 2023, and it has been so successful. We craft, laugh, sing, dance and have great fun!

Anyone is welcome to come to join our group, of any ability. Our group is called ‘Heart to Art’ the name of the group sums up what lovely sessions we have and what a lovely bunch of people come and join us.

🌟Station House Surgery Research team are taking part in another important UK-wide research trial called FluSNIFF toddler being led by University Hospital Southampton 🌟
🔎The aim of the study is to test if the nasal spray flu vaccine, currently offered to children aged two and over, can be safely extended to younger aged 12-23months. 👶
Flu can be serious for young children, and this needle-free vaccine – already used safely in older children – could make protection easier and more accessible.
👉 We are currently inviting parent and guardians of eligible toddlers to take part.

Text/Information to be posted:
We really value all feedback from our patients and their families, as well as our Friends & Family feedback which is completely anonymous. This helps us hear honestly what’s working well and what could be improved.

Sometimes, feedback includes specific situations that need further investigation. Because anonymous comments do not include your contact details, it can be difficult for us to follow up or fully resolve the issue.

If you want us to look into something in more detail, please speak to reception and leave your contact information. This allows us to investigate properly and ensure any necessary actions are taken.

Thank you for helping us make our service the best it can be!
